messages.subject: Identifiability Problems　in bi-factor model
parts:
Hi,

I'm studying bi-factor model and today I have a (unclear) question.

I think bifactor model belongs to so called hierarchical factor analysis model(sometimes higher order analysis model).

If so, don't parameter estimation in bifactor model have identifiability problems?

for example, we have to restrict item discrimination parameter in some item (at least 1 item) to 0 ?

But I also think that Gibbons&Hedeker (1992)' method;
 Gibbons&Hedeker (1992) say that the bifactor restriction reduces the s-dimensional integral in (4) to a two dimensional integral...

So, using  Gibbons&Hedeker (1992)' method, we don't have restrict a parameter in some item to 0? 

This question seems to be difficult to understand because of my lack of studies.

If you have some opinion, please give me that.

Thank you,

Yutaro

There are generally 2 ways to identify random variables: fix a slope to some constant (usually 1), or fix the variance to a constant (also to 1). Either will suffice for identification, and the latter is what Gibbons and Hedeker use to accomplish the dimensional reduction technique. Cheers.

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Identifiability Problems in bi-factor model
parts:
Yes. Computationally, standardized orthogonal integrals can be 'short formed' if you will to reduce computational complexity in high dimensional spaces. That's why in their solution no matter how many specific factors that are estimated, only 2 dimensional integration is required. But they aren't really taken to be N(0, 1) per say, that's just an identification constraint required (and is exactly the same as in structural equation modeling). 

Phil
